challenges.hint: Use “Refresh protocol” as a cue, then close the lesson again.

challenges.title: Prediction checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Choose one example or source file from this mission. Predict its behavior for a normal input and a changed or invalid input before running or revealing the reference. Explain the rule separating the outcomes.
challenges.hint: Change one condition at a time so the result teaches a rule.

challenges.prompt: Implement, debug, or adapt the mission exercise yourself. Record the acceptance criterion, command or interaction used to verify it, failure evidence, and one tradeoff. Do not paste the reference solution.
challenges.hint: A passing check, measured result, focused diff, or reproducible demo is stronger than ‘done.’

files.content:
# Bridge from the Existing Curriculum

Do not repeat all 263 projects before starting this track. Use this map to
refresh a concept only when the capstone exposes a weakness.

| Improved skill | Existing projects worth revisiting | Apply it by |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain decisions | JS 18, 31, 32, 40 | Extract board/card rules from HTTP and React |
| Async control | JS 42–44, 54, 84–85 | Bound work, cancel requests, handle stale replies |
| State and events | JS 38–41, 56, 59, 68, 83 | Define commands, events, versions, and projections |
| API composition | JS 60, 65–68, 76 | Build consistent routes, auth, realtime, rate limits |
| Parsing and trust boundaries | JS 34–36, 62, 69–72 | Validate runtime data and make errors actionable |
| Type modeling | TS 13, 23, 30, 32–43, 49–52 | Model DTOs, states, results, and branded identifiers |
| React behavior | React 13, 16–25, 37–44, 49, 51–60 | Build async, accessible, testable user journeys |
| C# service design | C# 14–24, 28, 32–36 | Use DI, middleware, auth, caching, workers, APIs |
| Interview algorithms | DSA 09–30 | Maintain fluency and explain complexity |

## Refresh protocol

When blocked:

1. Write the exact concept you cannot explain or implement.
2. Revisit at most two mapped exercises.
3. Re-implement their key idea without viewing the refactor.
4. Immediately apply the idea to the capstone.
5. Record the resulting commit as evidence in `PROGRESS.md`.

This prevents “preparing to prepare.” The capstone supplies the problem; the
existing curriculum supplies focused remediation.
